3_controllerStartsOnSelectedBuild.timing: daemon up 15:20:40Z; controller role claim recorded 15:30:52Z. In none mode nothing wakes the controller spawn except the daemon's own scheduled resync (resync_interval_seconds: 600): emitResync -> publishControllerEvent -> Envoy 404 no holder -> onUndeliverable -> ensureController. The spec/README say `the daemon starts its controller` without a time; the reviewer should expect the ~10-minute wait in none mode. In envoy mode the controller was up ~20 s after RIG READY because the root's issue.created event woke the spawn.

extraCheck.what: plan.json E2 asked for 0 hits of `failed to connect controller shim socket on ready`; observed 1 in the none run and 1 in the envoy run, plus 1 `failed to connect architect shim socket on ready for LEGSMOKE-47` in the envoy run — all `error: Worker RPC "negotiate_protocol" timed out after 5000ms`
extraCheck.rootCause: markControllerReady (processes.ts ~2670) is a best-effort shim connect at /controller/ready with worker_rpc_timeout_seconds=5; under the box's load (loadavg ~42/32 CPUs, 170+ omp processes) the freshly booted omp did not answer negotiate_protocol within 5 s. The same socket answered negotiate_protocol in 12 ms when probed read-only at 15:34:06Z (/tmp/legion10-smoke/probe-shim.ts; 138 backlog frames flushed). The controller's wakes travel over Envoy/NATS, not this socket, so the controller took its prompt and stayed alive; no crash, no `send did not invoke the agent`.
extraCheck.why_not_a_failure: Not one of spec acceptance 3's five evidence items; the planner derived the grep from LEGION-6 round 1 where the line coincided with the crash on the pinned build. Here every spec item holds and the crash message is absent. Daemon behaviour, nothing under scripts/smoke/ can change it. Reported to the architect (observationsForArchitect) for a decision on whether it needs its own issue.

notesForReviewer: Acceptance 3 in none mode needs the 600-second resync interval to elapse before a controller exists; do not read an empty roles map in the first ten minutes as a failure.

The three `failed to connect ... shim socket on ready` lines in the daemon logs are the 5-second negotiate_protocol timeout described under criteria.3.extraCheck, not the controller crash this PR fixes; the crash string `send did not invoke the agent` has zero hits everywhere.

When running `legion gh` or `jj git push` from a worker pane, never type your own `export LEGION_GRANT=...` line into a command: the harness prepends the real single-use grant, and a hand-typed second export overrides it and produces `Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT (403)`. That is what the implementer's `stale second LEGION_GRANT export` note was.
Both rigs are down; /tmp/legion10-smoke/* is left in place. Smoke roots LEGSMOKE-46 and LEGSMOKE-47 are set to done.
observationsForArchitect: Box-level flake, not this PR: ~/.omp/natives/18.1.15/ is one native-addon cache shared by every Oh My Pi build whose version starts 18.1.15; five distinct such builds were running concurrently (rpcfix, 20260908-220934, 20260910-001552, 20260910-044004, 20260910-172022) and each fresh start rewrites the file (mtimes 15:16:49, 15:17:38, 15:18:20, 15:20:40 with three different sizes). The rig daemon's boot probe died once on `Loaded ... pi_natives.linux-x64-modern.node but it does not expose the @oh-my-pi/pi-natives@18.1.15 version sentinel`. main has #954 (retry a boot probe that OMP died under) but this branch is based on 7db2cd83, before it; a rebase would give the rig daemon that retry. The spec's fail-closed probe design is fine; this is a machine hygiene issue (one natives dir per build) for the oh-my-pi side.

Daemon behaviour under load, not this PR: `Worker RPC "negotiate_protocol" timed out after 5000ms` at /controller/ready and at the architect's ready (worker_rpc_timeout_seconds default 5) with loadavg ~42; the socket answers in ~12 ms once omp is idle. For the controller and root architect this connect is best-effort, but phase workers receive their assignment over the same socket path (/worker/ready), so a 5 s timeout on this box may also delay or fail worker prompts. Worth its own issue or a config bump on this machine.

README gap (pre-existing, also noted by LEGION-6): the documented `secrets ... DISPATCH_TOKEN --` commands cannot run on this box because DISPATCH_TOKEN is not a secretsd key; the README's own alternative (~/.config/opencode/envoy.json .dispatch.token) works. Either add DISPATCH_TOKEN to secretsd or reword the two command blocks.

README claim `The daemon starts its controller` in none mode is true but only after the first scheduled resync (600 s). If a future tester needs a faster none-mode controller, `resync_interval_seconds` in the generated legion.yaml is the knob; not a defect against spec v13.

Two rigs cannot share a box: up.sh hard-codes the NATS container name legion-smoke-nats (ports are configurable, the name is not), and down.sh removes it by name. The LEGION-16 tester's concurrent rig blocked this run until they tore down. A per-SMOKE_PROJECT container name would remove the serialization; out of scope here.
